# Logos

> Logos is a small compiled language for software an agent writes and a human
> still has to trust. Allocation, fallible calls and release are visible in the
> source; the compiler refuses the rest. A failure arrives as a stable code and a
> node path, programs carry their own expectations, and the same source builds
> the same bytes. MIT, x86_64 and arm64 Linux, pre-1.0.

Repository: https://github.com/abaddon/logos (branch `main`, tag `v0.2.2`).
Language: prefix-form, every construct is `(head arg …)`. The compiler `logosc`
lowers Logos to LLVM IR text and `clang` links a C runtime, so a program is a
native Linux ELF with no interpreter. `logosc version` prints `logos 0.2.2`.

## Install and run

x86_64 Linux, glibc 2.35+, `clang` 14+ (needed at build time of every program).
Five commands, output pasted from a real run; full transcript in the quickstart.

```sh
gh release download v0.2.2 --repo abaddon/logos --pattern 'logos-*-x86_64-linux.tar.gz' --pattern SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
tar -xzf logos-0.2.2-x86_64-linux.tar.gz && cd logos-0.2.2-x86_64-linux
cat > hello.logos <<'EOF'
(mod hello)

(fn main :void ()
  (println "hello from logos"))
EOF
./bin/logosc build hello.logos -o hello && ./hello     # hello from logos
```

From a checkout instead: `git clone https://github.com/abaddon/logos && cd
logos`, then `./tools/logosc.sh build examples/hello.logos` and
`./build/hello` — the first call builds the compiler from `src/` (~50 s).

## Start here

- [docs/quickstart.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): the canonical walkthrough — tarball, checkout, a diagnostic read as data, a test run, the corpus, the gates; every output verified.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/AGENTS.md): the contributor contract — the six gates a change must pass, the four invariants, the regress rule, the bootstrap rule, pull-request rules.
- [docs/reference/agent-contract.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/agent-contract.md): the consumer contract — exit codes (0 success, 2 your source, 1 your machine), JSON shapes, determinism check, traps.
- [docs/install.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/install.md): download, checksum, unpack, and how the compiler finds its runtime and standard library from any working directory.
- [README.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/README.md): what Logos is, the status of the release, requirements, examples, layout.

## Language

- [docs/LOGOS.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/LOGOS.md): the generated manual — cheat sheet, one executable chapter per feature, reference tables. Generated from the compiler's tables; never edited by hand.
- [docs/reference/language.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/language.md): one page — the model, ten rules each with the diagnostic code it raises, a verified idiom per feature, what v1 refuses.
- [docs/reference/cli.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/cli.md): eight verbs, flags, exit codes, `--json` documents, artefact paths.
- [docs/reference/diagnostics.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/diagnostics.md): the diagnostic shapes, node paths, all 36 codes, retry policy.
- [docs/reference/stdlib.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/stdlib.md): all 21 standard-library functions (`io`, `str`, `map`) with signatures and ownership rules.
- [docs/reference/limits.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/reference/limits.md): every known limit in one page — read it before assuming a capability.
- `logosc guide --json`: the language as data. 96 forms, 16 types, 17 operators, 2 builtins, 36 diagnostic codes, 8 test categories, all under `schema_version: 1`.
- `logosc check FILE --json` and `logosc build FILE --json`: one JSON object per diagnostic, carrying `code` and `node_path`; hand the node path back to `logosc show FILE PATH` and the compiler prints that subtree.

## Examples

- [examples/agent-gate/](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/examples/agent-gate/README.md): a policy gate for an agent's tool calls in one 174-line file with nine `(test …)` nodes — the project to copy when starting something new. Run it from a checkout: `./tools/logosc.sh test examples/agent-gate/gate.logos` → `9 passed, 0 failed, 0 leaked`.
- [examples/wc.logos](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/examples/wc.logos): counts lines, words and bytes; matched against GNU `wc`.
- [examples/json.logos](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/examples/json.logos): a recursive-descent JSON parser and structural summary; matched against `jq`.
- [examples/matrix.logos](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/examples/matrix.logos): two 200x200 matrix multiplications on four threads; matched against a C reference.

## Contribute

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the short human route; every commit needs a `Signed-off-by` trailer matching its author.
- [docs/00-index.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/00-index.md): the full documentation index, one row per question.
- [docs/challenge/01-summary/program.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/challenge/01-summary/program.md): the Logos Agent Challenge — three tracks (build, land a pull request, port or teach), Round 1 opening 2026-12-01, no cash prizes.
- `bash tools/pr_gate.sh`: the six gates a pull request must pass, one PASS/FAIL line each. Agents and humans are held to the same gates.

## Optional

- [docs/history/build-ledger.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/history/build-ledger.md): the rulings behind the design, in order — the "why" the language cannot carry, because it has no comments.
- [docs/release.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/docs/release.md): how a release is built, proved reproducible and published.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/abaddon/logos/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what each version changed.
